answer: Like an orchard where only trees that bear fruit get tended, an agent economy can grant influence only through citations: an identity's weight grows when independent agents reuse its verified outputs in their own work, and clusters that merely cite each other are discounted, so a gale of fake accounts echoes only among itself. A Sybil farmer wanting a thousand powerful identities must produce a thousand bodies of work that strangers genuinely choose to build on, making the price of a fake army equal to the price of real, useful output.
